To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protection effectiveness of sparse vegetation in arid zones is dependent on the biomass type, height and distance from the biomass, and that the protection effectiveness is higher at the lower level and at distances of 0.5 to 1.5 times the tree height.
(1) The wind reduction ratio (R) was found to be a good parameter to quantify the wind protection effect of sparse biomass.
sparse vegetation can be used for wind erosion control, and the effectiveness depends on the height, the distance, the wind direction and the biomass species.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: a) the use of simple and inexpensive methods to quantify wind reduction around sparse biomass in arid areas; b) to assess the effectiveness and the potential of biomass to reduce the wind velocity and hence protect the ground surface and regions down wind from drifting sand and its consequences; c) to provide a basis for further research in the field of wind erosion control.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protection provided by biomass is a function of its height and the distance to the object to be protected, and that it is more effective in the prevailing wind and less effective in the perpendicular direction.
the protection of the biomass was better in terms of wind reduction than in terms of protection index (E).
the biomass used in this study, which is common to arid zone, can reduce the wind force (velocity), hence protecting the surface and regions from drifting sand and its consequences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it showed that sparse biomass in a desertified environment can be effective in wind reduction and protection.
it has shown that biomass can be used as a wind erosion protection measure.
sparse vegetation can provide protection from wind erosion and that it is important to know how to quantify this protection and to know the limits of the protection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sparse vegetation, common in arid zones, can be used as wind protection.
sparse vegetation is a very important factor in the control of wind erosion and that its role is not sufficiently appreciated in Africa.
